Contextual toolbox: Adjust, Retouch and Privacy

Implemented 16 October 2026. Native hosted screenshots of isolated synthetic projects, not mockups or captures of personal photos. Mac captures use a borderless test window; mobile captures use controlled viewports and include portrait, landscape and accessibility text. Tap an image to enlarge. Images are resized and JPEG-compressed for this standalone report; native PNG attachments remain in the test result bundles.

Mac and landscape iPad keep a narrow tool rail. Adjust exposes one chosen parameter with Quick Fix and optional full properties. Retouch exposes Heal/Clone, brush size and source selection. Privacy exposes Draw/Select, Pixelate and Freeform. Detailed settings are optional; they no longer reserve a full column when these tools first open. Portrait iPad and phone place controls directly above the bottom toolbox. Phone landscape uses a side rail and a zoom menu. Existing source geometry, processing, draft history and operation inputs are retained.

The earlier stacked top tool rows are removed. Batch properties retain their separate visibility preference. Accessibility text uses a compact settings entry with readable detailed controls, single-line Apply/Cancel and a zoom menu.

Verification and limits

  • Core: 117 tests passed.
  • Focused Mac checks: 22 passed, including native captures and combined Retouch/Privacy draft Apply, Undo/Redo and stable batch inputs.
  • Focused iPhone and iPad checks: 22 passed each, including portrait, landscape, largest-text captures, missing-image handling and keyboard-stable layout tests.
  • Unsigned Release builds: macOS and iOS/iPadOS passed. Signing was not changed.
  • Release-tool tests: 2 passed. Static preflight has zero failures and four distribution blockers: public support/privacy URL verification and two distribution signatures.

Live iPhone Simulator checks confirmed Retouch settings opening and closing, source selection availability, and switching to Privacy with Pixelate/Freeform. Device Hub orientation rendering was inconsistent, so controlled native captures are the layout evidence. Physical-device touch, Pencil, keyboard, VoiceOver and performance validation remain. This was a focused validation run, not a claim that the entire native suite is clean; the previously reported long Mac capture exception was not retested here. Some builds encountered concurrent Demo Workspace integration while files were being added; final builds passed with that work preserved.
